author: TEDx Talks
description:
Why can one room make you feel bold while another leaves you guarded? Design futurist Meena Krenek takes us from a childhood bedsheet fort to a high-stakes business meeting to explore the quiet influence of the spaces we enter every day. Meena Krenek has spent her career designing spaces around one conviction: Rooms don't simply hold our lives. They shape them. 

An award-winning design director, Meena creates environments that strengthen culture and forge emotional connections between people and place. For more than two decades, she has brought architecture and interior design together across workplaces, stadiums, restaurants and other spaces, using design to influence how people feel, move, connect and experience an organization.

At the heart of Meena's work is human experience. Rather than designing spaces simply to look beautiful, she considers what they communicate, how they tell a story and, ultimately, what they ask of the people who inhabit them. This talk was given at a TEDx
title: What is your room telling you? | Meena Krenek | TEDxAtlanta

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The first recorded resume was written more than 500 years ago, and the way we hire hasn’t changed much since. HR tech veteran Matt Baxter argues that today’s hiring system buries the signal in noise for job seekers and employers alike, and he challenges both to look past the bullet points for what really matters. Matt Baxter is an entrepreneur and HR tech founder who believes the resume is noise. He started his first company, Stony Pointe Lawn Care, at 15, ran it for six years, and sold it in 2015 while studying management at Hope College.

Frustrated by the friction of frontline hiring, he wanted a faster, more human way to see who a candidate actually is. So he co-founded Wedge, an asynchronous video interviewing platform built to replace the phone screen. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Resume is Noise | Matt Baxter | TEDxMacatawa

author: TEDx Talks

But after the 2025 election defunded the long-term grant she’d been leading, she embraced a new chapter online. She now builds a lifestyle social media platform in real time, sharing authentic stories of how she is building her fulfilling life with an audience that’s growing right along with her. Taylor Krause is a full-time content creator who many first met on Netflix’s Love Is Blind, but her story reaches far beyond reality TV. Before cameras ever entered the picture, Taylor spent nearly a decade working in climate and clean energy policy, driven by a passion for meaningful, long-term impact. She earned her master’s degree in Energy Policy from Johns Hopkins University and was serving as federal policy manager at a leading think tank, where she was an
title: Xperiment - Taylor Krause | Taylor Krause | TEDxBerkeley

author: TEDx Talks
description: My talk explores failure not as an identity, but as information. Through the metaphor of a book with a missing page and personal experiences of loss, rejection, change, and rebuilding, I, Anshu Joshi Singh invite the audience to rethink what failure means. The talk explores the difference between “I failed” and “I am a failure,” the importance of letting go of outdated dreams and identities, and the power of choosing what comes next. At its heart, the message is simple: we may not control what happens to us, but we retain the authorship to decide what the next chapter of our lives will be Anshu Joshi Singh is an author, life coach, author coach, NLP practitioner, motivational speaker, entrepreneur, and publishing professional who helps people navigate change with greater clarity, confidence, and self-awareness. As a life coach, she works closely with individuals on identity, relationships, motherhood, midlife, emotional well-being, and personal growth.She has authored 15 books, includ
title: The Missing Page - How to Fail Without Becoming a Failure | Anshu Joshi Singh | TEDxIPEC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Jasmine Ornish is an independent researcher exploring the ethical frontier opened by Project CETI, a nonprofit initiative using AI and bioacoustics to study sperm whale communication. Mentored by CETI founder and marine biologist Dr. David Gruber, she created an interdisciplinary independent study and co-authored a paper examining humanity’s responsibilities if we begin to understand another species more deeply. Jasmine Ornish is an independent researcher at the intersection of artificial intelligence, interspecies communication, and ethics. Her inquiry is grounded in Project CETI, the Cetacean Translation Initiative, a nonprofit founded by marine biologist and National Geographic Explorer Dr. David Gruber. By combining machine learning with bioacoustics, linguistics, robotics, and field research, CETI is uncovering patterns in sperm whale codas previously beyond unaided human perception.

Jasmine created an interdisciplinary independent study examining the questions this work raises
title: Xperiment - Jasmine Ornish | Jasmine Ornish | TEDxBerkeley

author: TEDx Talks
description: Patrick Poole is a research physicist at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, where he works with some of the world’s most powerful lasers to explore the behavior of matter under extreme conditions. Beyond his research, Patrick is passionate about making science accessible to everyone, from developing the next generation of fusion energy scientists to bringing scientific demonstrations to audiences of all ages. Patrick Poole is a Research Physicist at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), where he conducts plasma physics experiments at the National Ignition Facility (NIF), the world’s largest and most energetic laser system. At LLNL Patrick’s research spans high-energy-density (HED) and plasma physics, including materials science under extreme x-ray and neutron irradiation, radiography of complex hydrodynamic phenomena, photonics based on novel plasma optics, and high-average-power laser and experiment development for extreme ultraviolet lithography. Patrick also serves as
title: Xperiment - Patrick Poole | Patrick Poole | TEDxBerkeley

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Before we speak, most of us quietly calculate what’s safe to say, and when we do speak, we argue to win. Cecilia Puente makes the case that conversations that matter ask us to take three risks: being heard, being wrong, and being changed. Drawing on the ancient Greek idea of parrhesia, she shows how courage, curiosity, and openness can turn disagreement into discovery. Cecilia Puente is a high school junior, writer, and youth leader interested in how we communicate across differences. She has shared her writing and ideas through essays, competitions, and public forums. Through programs at Georgetown, Harvard, and the University of Chicago, she has studied courageous discourse, public speaking, debate, and approaches to building connected communities. She has carried these experiences into national youth boards and civic leadership initiatives, and is creating opportunities for dialogue in her community.

Cecilia also mentors younger students and studied ballet for over a decade. She i
title: The Conversations That Could Change Us | Cecilia Puente | TEDxMacatawa

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the most dangerous thing you can give a child is an immediate answer? After losing her aunt to pancreatic cancer, student researcher Nina Shaye taught herself machine learning to build an AI model that detects early-stage tumors, and learned what AI can’t do. She makes the case that purpose, choice, and wonder are what make us human in an age of instant answers. Nina Shaye is a junior at the Kalamazoo Area Math and Science Center and Portage Central High School. Passionate about both STEM and the arts, she conducts research in machine learning and cancer detection and has presented her work at international research conferences, including the International Science and Engineering Fair and International Youth Research Conference.

Nina is also an accomplished visual artist, having won the Congressional Art Competition and received multiple Scholastic Gold Keys. She is deeply involved in the West Michigan community and founded Ladybug Art Camp, which introduces young girls in Ka
title: When Intelligence Becomes Artificial, What Makes Us Human? | Nina Shaye | TEDxMacatawa

author: TEDx Talks
description:
¿Qué sucede cuando el lugar donde naces, tu origen y las costumbres de tu comunidad parecen determinar lo que puedes o no puedes llegar a ser? Eufrosina Cruz comparte la historia de una niña indígena zapoteca a quien la vida le negó oportunidades desde el principio: crecer en un entorno donde las mujeres estaban destinadas a servir, obedecer y convertirse en madres desde muy pequeñas. Pero también es la historia de alguien que decidió cuestionar aquello que parecía normal y dejar de aceptar que su origen definiera su destino.
A través de sus experiencias, reflexiona sobre el poder de la educación, la palabra y las pequeñas decisiones que permiten desafiar las desigualdades. Desde aprender a cuestionar su entorno hasta abrirse camino en espacios donde le dijeron que no podía estar, su historia nos invita a reconocer que la costumbre no justifica la violencia ni la injusticia, y que los derechos no deberían depender del lugar donde nacemos. Porque cambiar una historia también significa
title: Los derechos que la vida me negó | Eufrosina Cruz | TEDxUJED

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if feeling our deepest emotions is the key to reconnecting with ourselves and with life?
In this deeply personal TEDx Talk, actress Leonor Varela explores emotional awareness, vulnerability, grief, and the courage it takes to feel what we fear most.
Through the loss of her son Matteo, Leonor discovers that avoiding emotional pain can disconnect us from ourselves, while allowing ourselves to feel can open the door to self-love, healing, and a deeper experience of human connection.
A reflection on grief and loss, emotional healing, the mind-body connection, and what it means to be truly alive. Sometimes, the place we fear entering is where love is still waiting for us. Leonor Varela is an internationally recognized actress and dedicated activist. She is also a prominent Chilean cultural figure and mother. Varela is the author of the memoir, "Ir al cielo y Volver" (Go to Heaven and Back), sharing her profound personal journey. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED confer
title: I Feel, Therefore I Am | Leonor Varela | TEDxFrutillar

author: TEDx Talks
description: From cruise control to kidneys to the Federal Reserve, every stable system runs on the same hidden architecture: cybernetics. Drew Morgan breaks down four core concepts (feedback, feed forward, lag, and saturation) and shows how to use them to build steadier systems at work and in life. Drew is a Park Township based engineer, maker, and sometimes artist who has also lived in the South and on the other (salty) West coast. He enjoys the intersection of the profound with the absurd. He strives for delightful form and satisfying function in everything he does, especially when it’s unexpected. He spends his time working for Disher Engineering in Zeeland, pursuing curiosity, tinkering, and exploring West Michigan with his wife and two daughters. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Cybernetics and You! | Drew Morgan | TEDxMacatawa

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Ask 10 people what’s causing the housing crisis and you’ll get 10 different answers. Chris Marco separates housing myths from housing realities, takes a road trip through communities already building solutions, and shows why fixing a national problem starts at your local planning commission. Chris Marco is the first-ever Director of Community Development at Lakeshore Advantage, where he supports housing initiatives in Allegan and Ottawa counties. A 26-year native of West Michigan, Chris cares deeply about the region’s communities and the people who call them home.

Chris has previously presented at the International Conference on Urban Affairs and the Midwest Political Science Association. He has also delivered guest lectures and published research in Governing Magazine, Public Square: A CNU Journal, and The Urbanist. A proud Laker for a Lifetime, Chris holds degrees in Public Administration and Political Science from Grand Valley State University. This talk was given at a TEDx event
title: Demystifying the Housing Crisis | Chris Marco | TEDxMacatawa

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Across our economy, thousands of successful SMEs face an invisible crisis: there is no one to take over when their founders step down.

While our culture glorifies starting from scratch, the real question is: Who is brave enough to take the baton and carry a legacy forward? 

This is the mission of the "Re-Founder"-entrepreneurs who choose to reinvent what already works rather than reinventing the wheel. 

Yet, true succession is never a lone-wolf journey. It requires strong ecosystems, collaborative teams, and the courage to unite tradition with fresh innovation. 

By stepping up together to lead existing companies, we do not just preserve a lifetime's work - we secure the very backbone of our future economy. Marcel Gertsch leads M&A and advisory projects for SMEs, specializing in navigating complex corporate successions and strategic growth. He is passionate about turning the looming succession crisis into a major economic opportunity for new leaders. Through his work, Marcel champi
title: Don’t Start a Startup: Become a Re-Founder | Marcel Gertsch | TEDxHWZ Studio

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Rafa Carbajal plantea una pregunta urgente: ¿cómo podemos hacer que la ciencia llegue a las personas en una época donde la desinformación se viraliza más rápido que la evidencia? En un mundo donde los algoritmos premian las respuestas fáciles, las emociones y los contenidos que generan polémica, comunicar conocimiento científico se ha convertido en un desafío.
A través de experiencias personales y ejemplos cotidianos, Rafa cuestiona la influencia de los gurús de internet, las falsas soluciones y las barreras que enfrentan quienes buscan comunicar ciencia en redes sociales. Su propuesta es recuperar algo esencial: la curiosidad, la empatía y la capacidad de cuestionar. Porque no se trata solamente de combatir la desinformación, sino de encontrar nuevas formas de despertar el interés por la ciencia y acercarla a todos.
 Es ingeniero bioquímico, con maestría y doctorado en Ingeniería Bioquímica, especializado en biotecnología microbiana. Es profesor e investigador del Tecnológico Naciona
title: Hablar de ciencia en la era del algoritmo | Rafa Carbajal | TEDxUJED

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the words you speak to someone today could change what they believe about themselves tomorrow? 
As a child, Laurie Lynn was called names at home and on the playground that made her question her worth. Some labels she fought against; others she believed and became a part of her identity. It wasn't until decades later that she discovered just how deeply our words and what we believe about ourselves can shape the way we see ourselves. And how a few simple words from someone who believed in her could change everything.
Through a series of heartfelt, humorous and personal stories, Laurie Lynn explores the extraordinary power of belief and the lasting impact of the words we speak into one another's lives. From a mentor who helped her see herself differently, to a daughter who received those same powerful words to become a champion and then passed those same words on to her teammates, Laurie reveals how belief can be given, received, and carried forward. Because words have a way of c
title: YOU have the POWER! | Laurie Lynn | TEDxTinley Park

What if you've spent years trying to fix something about yourself that was never broken?

At 19, Solomon believed his appearance made him less worthy of confidence. He hid behind a hat, carried himself differently, and struggled to feel comfortable in his own skin. His experience taught him an important lesson: the way we see ourselves can profoundly influence the way we live.

But years later, a heartbreaking encounter with someone battling deep self-loathing revealed that negative self-perception can have consequences far beyond appearance or confidence.

In this talk, Solomon invites us to examine the stories we tell ourselves, question the beliefs that limit us,
title: What If You're Wrong About Yourself? | Solomon Asine | TEDxTinley Park

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What becomes possible when we stop believing that someone else has to matter less for us to matter?

Growing up in China during the one-child policy era, Muxiang Pajerski was devalued as a third daughter. She learned a zero-sum equation of belonging: for one person to be valued, another had to be devalued. Years later, she faced that same equation when she fell in love with a man whose life already included three teenage children and a best friend who was also his ex-wife.

Through a Chinese dress, an Easter invitation, and two wine glasses, two women expected to be rivals built trust one respectful move at a time. Their relationship gave their children the freedom to love without choosing sides and showed that a family can grow without anyone losing their place.

In this personal and heartfelt talk, Muxiang challenges us to look beyond labels, recognize the different roles people play, and make room for another person’s importance without surrendering our own place. Someone else can
title: Why I bought my husband’s ex-wife wine glasses on my honeymoon | Muxiang Pajerski | TEDxTinley Park

author: TEDx Talks
description:
O que faz uma cidade ser verdadeiramente inteligente? A quantidade de tecnologias que utiliza ou a capacidade de conectar as pessoas que vivem nela?

Para Marcelo Verly, o futuro das cidades não depende apenas de grandes obras, equipamentos modernos ou sistemas de informação. Depende, sobretudo, da capacidade de escutar, conectar e mobilizar pessoas em torno de objetivos comuns.

Nesta palestra, Marcelo apresenta o conceito de inteligência invisível das cidades: o conhecimento, as experiências e as relações humanas que existem nos territórios, mas que nem sempre encontram oportunidades de se conectar.

A partir de sua trajetória na educação e na gestão pública, ele relembra um dos momentos mais desafiadores de sua vida profissional: a tragédia climática de 2011, quando atuava como secretário municipal de Educação de Nova Friburgo.

Diante de uma rede escolar profundamente atingida, a reconstrução exigiu muito mais do que recursos materiais. Exigiu colaboração, compromisso coletivo e a
title: Cidades pensadas com pessoas no centro | Marcelo Verly | TEDxPraça Getúlio Vargas

author: TEDx Talks
description: We often associate social media with distraction and wasted time, yet our attention remains trapped there. Guillermo proposes poetry as an alternative to the fleeting pleasures of screens. It isn't easy, but he argues that its beauty has the power to wake us up and change society. Guillermo is 17. He devotes a large part of his time to sports—specifically running, where he competes at the national level. This requires great consistency and effort, something he takes pride in. He has always been a lover of literature, another habit to which he devotes much of his time, and in recent years, he has focused increasingly on poetry. In his TEDx talk, he uses the core concept of poetry to cut through the noise generated by social media and short-term pleasures. In a society driven by the allure of technology, the beauty of poetry emerges, shifting our attention toward something beautiful and enduring. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organ
title: Poetry in a Noisy World | Guillermo Gala | TEDxIES Saramago Majadahonda Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Quinze anos depois da tragédia climática de 2011, Nova Friburgo e a Região Serrana do Rio de Janeiro estão realmente mais preparadas para enfrentar novos desastres?

Em janeiro de 2011, chuvas intensas e deslizamentos marcaram profundamente a história da região. Famílias perderam pessoas queridas, comunidades foram atingidas e milhares de moradores precisaram reconstruir suas vidas.

Nesta palestra, a jornalista e professora universitária Gabriella Bini revisita essa memória coletiva para propor uma reflexão que vai além do passado: o que aprendemos e, principalmente, o que fizemos com esse aprendizado?

A partir de sua experiência na comunicação, Gabriella destaca o papel fundamental do rádio e dos radioamadores durante a tragédia, quando a falta de energia elétrica e as dificuldades de comunicação tornaram ainda mais importante a circulação de informações e a mobilização da população.

Ela também questiona se os alertas e as orientações chegaram às comunidades mais vulneráveis e cha
title: A comunicação que transforma dor em reconstrução | Gabriella Bini | TEDxPraça Getúlio Vargas

author: TEDx Talks
description: Marta explores how finding the right words to describe our emotions and experiences can transform the way we understand ourselves and the world around us, combining science with personal experience. Marta is a 17-year-old IB student at IES José Saramago in Madrid. She is passionate about science, but above all about understanding the world around her, especially language and communication. Combining science with personal experience, her talk explores how finding the right words for our emotions and experiences can change the way we understand ourselves and the world. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Power of Naming Things | Marta Roa | TEDxIES Saramago Majadahonda Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: We spend a lot of time on social media, and the celebrities we follow and admire can easily shape the way we see things. Guillermina talks about the influence famous people have on their followers and invites us to discover where their voice ends and ours begins. Guillermina is a 17-year-old student in her second year of the IB Diploma Programme at IES José Saramago. Born and raised in Spain, she is half Italian. She has always been curious about the influence celebrities have over so many people, especially through social media. Her talk explores how the famous people we admire shape the way we see things, and where their voice ends and ours begins. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Living in Someone Else's Spotlight | Guillermina Dall'Acqua | TEDxIES Saramago Majadahonda Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Spending a year abroad changed the way Emma sees life: she learned to seize every opportunity, value other points of view and live each day as if it were her last. She shares the mindset this experience gave her and encourages us to look at life more positively and openly, step out of our comfort zone and make the most of everything we experience. Emma is a 17-year-old student who is naturally curious about how the world works. She loves learning about other cultures and languages, and about the politics, history and art that have shaped society. A year as an exchange student in Ireland changed the way she sees life, teaching her to embrace every opportunity and value different perspectives. In her talk, she shares that mindset and encourages others to step out of their comfort zone. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Stepping Out of Your Comfort Zone | Emma Pascau | TEDxIES Saramago Majadahonda Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In adolescence, emotions can be so intense that words are not enough to express them. Rocío proposes art and painting as an answer: telling our stories through strokes of colour improves our wellbeing, helps us understand ourselves and connects us with people around the world. Even doodling in our notes sparks creativity and helps build our identity. Rocío is a 17-year-old student from Madrid in her final year of secondary school. Passionate and outgoing, she discovered a love of public speaking through debating competitions and enjoys the way communication brings people together and gives ideas a voice. Like many teenagers, she is still working out what her future holds. Her talk brings together two things she cares about: understanding the world and finding creative ways to express what words cannot capture. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Art of Being a Teenager | Rocío García Uría | TEDxIES Saramago Majadahonda Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Em janeiro de 2011, uma das maiores tragédias climáticas da história do Brasil atingiu a Região Serrana do Rio de Janeiro. Em meio à destruição, Wellington Guimarães viveu uma experiência que transformaria para sempre sua relação com a vida, a fé e a capacidade de escutar.

Soterrado ao lado da esposa e do filho de apenas sete meses, Wellington enfrentou horas de incerteza, perdeu sua companheira e sobreviveu com o bebê a uma situação extrema.

Nesta palestra, ele compartilha os acontecimentos daquela noite e relata como uma voz interior, que interpreta como uma manifestação divina, o orientou em momentos decisivos para sua sobrevivência.

A experiência também marcou o início de uma profunda jornada de reconstrução pessoal, espiritual e familiar.

Ao revisitar essa trajetória, Wellington propõe uma reflexão sobre algo que acredita estar desaparecendo da vida contemporânea: nossa capacidade de escutar.

Entre compromissos, responsabilidades, tecnologias e uma rotina cada vez mais acele
title: A voz que ouvi quando tudo desmoronou | Wellington Guimarães | TEDxPraça Getúlio Vargas

author: TEDx Talks
description: We tend to think of exercise as something that mainly looks after the body. Combining scientific research with her own experience as an athlete, Manuela reveals the powerful impact physical activity also has on our brain, our emotions and the way we face challenges. Manuela has played volleyball since she was eight and has been involved in sport since the age of five. Along the way she has learned that exercise goes far beyond physical fitness: sport has helped her face challenges, manage her emotions and grow both on and off the court. In her talk, she invites the audience to see physical activity from a new perspective and make it part of their lives. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Mind in the Game | Manuela Caparrós | TEDxIES Saramago Majadahonda Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Jorge Acevedo plantea una pregunta fundamental: ¿para quién estamos construyendo y a quién estamos dejando fuera de las decisiones que transforman nuestras ciudades? Porque levantar edificios, construir carreteras o desarrollar grandes proyectos no necesariamente significa mejorar la vida de las personas.
A través de experiencias en proyectos de infraestructura y desarrollo urbano, cuestiona una visión del progreso centrada en cifras, inversiones y rentabilidad, para poner sobre la mesa algo que suele olvidarse: las personas que habitarán, utilizarán y dependerán de aquello que construimos. Desde una perspectiva humana, social y ética, nos invita a repensar el significado del desarrollo y a entender que una obra puede terminar con su inauguración, pero el verdadero desarrollo comienza cuando transforma una vida.
 Es empresario mexicano y especialista en el desarrollo de proyectos de alto impacto económico y social. A lo largo de su trayectoria ha impulsado proyectos con un valor super
title: ¿Para qué construimos? Construir no es desarrollar | Jorge Acevedo Alarid | TEDxUJED

author: TEDx Talks
description: Drawing on her passion for history, literature and philosophy, Nadia shows that the ideas that changed the world were born not from comfort but from restlessness. She defends peaceful revolution as an ongoing necessity for building a fairer society, and reminds us that our privileges should never stop us from questioning the world: today's freedoms were yesterday's revolutions. Nadia is a 17-year-old student in her second year of the IB Diploma Programme at IES José Saramago. She has competed in rhythmic gymnastics at national level since the age of six and sings in a choir. Her lifelong interest in literature, philosophy, history and politics shapes her talk, which explores why questioning the world is essential to building a fairer society. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Choice to Question | Nadia Vilsan | TEDxIES Saramago Majadahonda Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: For a long time, María chased perfection, believing it would bring her calm and control. Instead, it brought anxiety and a fear of making mistakes. She shares how she came to see imperfection not as a failure but as what connects us to others, helps us learn and lets us enjoy life with less pressure. María is a curious and ambitious student with a passion for mathematics and science, as well as for art, especially ballet and fashion. Always determined to give her best, she began to wonder where the line lies between wanting to improve and expecting ourselves to be perfect. Drawing on psychology, neuroscience and her own experience, her talk shows why imperfection is not a weakness but an essential part of being human. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Imperfection: The Beauty in the Broken | María Párraga | TEDxIES Saramago Majadahonda Youth
